newsitem.title: USA: Interim Services pays $574 million for Britain's Michael Page.
newsitem.headline: Interim Services pays $574 million for Britain's Michael Page.

text.p: Interim Services Inc., continuing its expansion into global markets, said Monday it offered $574 million in cash to acquire Michael Page Group Plc, a British-based provider of professional recruitment and temporary employment services worldwide.

"We are aligning ourselves with what we believe is the preeminent staffing and recruiting company operating outside of North America," Interim Services President and Chief Executive Ray Marcy said in a statement announcing the offer.
Interim, based in Ft. Lauderdale, Fla., is already a staffing and employment industry leader with some 1,000 offices in North America and Europe.

It said in an announcement made in London that it had made a tender offer to purchase all outstanding shares of Michael Page for 5.57 pounds ($9.07) a share, including a dividend to be paid to Page shareholders for 1996.
Interim said the offer represented a 12.5 percent premium over Page's closing price Friday.
The company said its acquisition of Page, which is expected to be completed by June, will add slightly to its earnings this year and contribute "significantly" to income next year.
Interim said it will finance the purchase under a $675 million loan facility provided by NationsBank, which will allow it to continue to make smaller, selective acquisitions.
Interim described Michael Page as a premier international recruiting and staffing company, specialising in the fields of accounting, finance, technology, sales and marketing.

It has 40 offices in Britain, France, Germany, The Netherlands, Australia, Hong Kong and Singapore, with its business equally split between temporary staffing and full-time placement. A significant number of its clients are large international banks and financial institutions.
Iterim said Michael Page will operate as a subsidiary, with Chief Executive Terry Benson and Finance Director Ian Nash retaining their positions.
Iterim's stock added $1.625 to $39.375 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
